about: Measured value of the usefulness score's anchor weights (sim/analyze/calibrate.py). Each anchor is given to team 0 and the change in its result is measured against the same seeds without it; value.py derives its weights from this file (sim/policies/calibration.py).
recipients: 50% of the eligible players of team 0, rounded up, at least one (a State: that many applications on random enemies); changes are per unit
result: team 0: win 1, draw 0.5, loss 0; paired by seed

map_flags.fair: Nothing positional drives this anchor's value; the measurement stands.
map_flags.may-overstate: Wins melee. Without a map melee decides most games (casters can't keep distance or kite), so this may read high against ranged and control anchors. Used as measured.
map_flags.may-understate: Part of the value is positional and Phase 1 has no space, so the calibrated weight is used only above the hand weight (a floor).
map_flags.needs-map: The engine gives this no effect without a map; the measurement is recorded but the hand weight is used (uncalibrated, needs map).

kill.unit: a use of Finger of Death per life
kill.why: The reference: 20' range is a probability, and a kill is a kill.

armor.unit: a point of armor on every location
armor.why: Worn armor only matters in melee and against arrows.

armor-3-bare.unit: a point of armor, 0 to 3 for a fighter wearing none
armor-3-bare.why: What Berserker's 'may not wear armor' takes from a Barbarian in 3 points.

magic-armor.unit: Magic Armor 1 on a fighter, every life
magic-armor.why: Like worn armor; it goes to front-line fighters in play.

heal.why: Wounds cost little in Phase 1: most of a wound's cost in play is mobility (a leg wound means kneeling), which needs a map; an arm wound's lost shield is modeled.

heal-fighter.unit: a Heal per life held by a fighter
heal-fighter.why: A Heal's value to a fighter, by how fighters use it: they are rarely out of melee while wounded (0.04-0.08 casts per life of an Unlimited self-Heal), so this is a use discount and is not floored like the Heal anchor.

revive.unit: a Raise Dead per refresh (per game in annihilation)
revive.why: Reaching the body is a probability; Raise Dead's heal and drawbacks are subtracted.

death-ward.unit: one death prevented per life (Phoenix Tears' way)

wound-ball.why: As for Heal: a wound's cost in play is mostly mobility. Force Bolt's specials add nothing to its wound in the engine (a ball's Armor Breaking turns a hit on light armor into lost armor, not a wound; weapon-destroying from a ball isn't modeled), so its whole score is the wound's.

state-stunned.unit: stunned for 30 s on a random enemy
state-stunned.why: Can't act and is easy to hit: both modeled.

state-frozen.unit: frozen for 30 s on a random enemy
state-frozen.why: Phase 1 counts the time out of the fight, not a lane or ground left open.

state-stopped.unit: stopped for 30 s on a random enemy
state-stopped.why: Nothing stops a Stopped player closing to melee in Phase 1: no effect at all.

state-suppressed.unit: suppressed for 30 s on a random enemy

state-fragile.unit: fragile for 30 s on a random enemy
state-fragile.why: Dies on the next wound: modeled.

state-insubstantial.unit: insubstantial for 30 s on a random enemy
state-insubstantial.why: Out of the fight for the time; a map would add where they are.

armor-breaking.unit: Armor Breaking on a fighter's weapon, every life

wounds-kill.unit: Wounds Kill on a fighter's weapon, every life

free-charge.unit: an instant Charge of a spent chargeable ability
free-charge.why: Per Charge actually made; compared with what value.py says a refill is worth.

charge-time.unit: a second of Charge incantation saved
charge-time.why: Per second actually saved. With a map a player Charges behind the line; Phase 1 lets fighters Charge only in a lull.

extra-slot.unit: an extra Enchantment slot on a fighter
extra-slot.why: Teammates fill it; compared with the whole value of the Enchantment that fills it.
